original_question: Can one obtain rigorous explicit formulas for Tracy-Widom distribution functions for general beta-ensembles beyond the classical invariant cases beta = 1, 2, and 4, including a rigorous completion of Rumanov's approach for all even beta > 0 and a rigorous verification of the asymptotic formulas proposed by Borot, Eynard, Majumdar, and Nadal for general beta > 0?
target_in_paper: Problem 2 (universality for random matrix theory (RMT)), specifically the unnumbered open-problem paragraph on pp. 5–6 about explicit Tracy–Widom formulae for general β-ensembles, Rumanov's β=6/even-β program, and the Borot–Eynard–Majumdar–Nadal asymptotic formulas. ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2017/016/sigma17-016.pdf))
correct_elements: The draft is already very close to Deift's actual target: it identifies explicit Tracy–Widom formulae for general β-ensembles as the main problem, correctly singles out the classical cases β=1, 2, and 4 as the only explicit cases known at the time, correctly isolates Rumanov's approach as the key nonclassical development, and correctly includes rigorous verification of the Borot–Eynard–Majumdar–Nadal asymptotic formulas as the second open challenge. ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2017/016/sigma17-016.pdf))
missing_details: The paper is specifically about the Tracy–Widom distribution attached to β-ensembles at the spectral edge; a stand-alone formulation should identify the object as the limiting distribution function F_β of the centered and scaled top eigenvalue, rather than just saying Tracy–Widom distribution functions in the abstract. Deift assumes this background rather than restating it. ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2017/016/sigma17-016.pdf))

The quantification should be fixed-β: the paragraph speaks of the distribution for each β and of asymptotic formulas for general β>0, not of a uniform-in-β statement. ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2017/016/sigma17-016.pdf))

The phrase all even β>0 is implicit arithmetic language; to make the question precise, it should be read as all positive even integers β = 2, 4, 6, .... The draft leaves this ambiguity unresolved. This clarification is an inference from the paper's wording, not a separately stated hypothesis. ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2017/016/sigma17-016.pdf))

Rumanov's existing nonclassical formula is not just any formula: Deift specifies that the β = 6 Tracy–Widom distribution is represented in terms of Painlevé II and an auxiliary ODE, and that this is the approach to be completed rigorously and extended. ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2017/016/sigma17-016.pdf))

Deift's paragraph has a two-part structure that should be preserved: first, rigorous explicit formulas via the Rumanov line of attack; second, rigorous verification of the detailed asymptotic formulas obtained by Borot, Eynard, Majumdar, and Nadal for general β > 0. ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2017/016/sigma17-016.pdf))

There are no ambient-ring, homogeneity, degree, or nilpotency conditions in this problem; the real hidden assumptions are the β-ensemble/Tracy–Widom setting, edge scaling, and the fixed-β quantifiers. ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2017/016/sigma17-016.pdf))
refined_question: If F_β(s) denotes the Tracy–Widom distribution function for β-ensembles at the spectral edge for a fixed β > 0, can one rigorously obtain explicit formulae for F_β beyond the classical invariant cases β = 1, 2, and 4, in particular by putting Rumanov's β = 6 representation in terms of Painlevé II and an auxiliary ODE on a fully rigorous footing and extending that program to every positive even integer β, and can one rigorously prove the detailed asymptotic formulas for F_β proposed by Borot, Eynard, Majumdar, and Nadal for all β > 0? ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2017/016/sigma17-016.pdf))
justification: Deift presents the relevant statement as an informal open problem inside Problem 2. The paragraph first identifies the long-standing problem of finding explicit Tracy–Widom formulae for general β-ensembles, then singles out Rumanov's β = 6 construction and its in-principle extension to even β, and finally isolates rigorous verification of the Borot–Eynard–Majumdar–Nadal asymptotic formulas for general β > 0. The refined question keeps exactly that scope and does not broaden the problem to unrelated β-ensemble, bulk, or universality questions. ([sigma-journal.com](https://sigma-journal.com/2017/016/sigma17-016.pdf))
